first_impression.reaction: Googled 'santorini wedding' because it's one of the places we're weighing up. The intro is an order of decisions, not a sunset sales pitch, so I kept going. Went straight to the FAQ and the cost section as usual. The cost section is thinner than I'd like, but it does name a real catch: some venues make you hire a planner, and 'exclusive use' can mean the spaces you book, not the hotel. The weather table admits there's no station on Santorini and uses Naxos instead, and the page tells me about earthquakes, wildfires and ferry cancellations. That's a business not hiding the downsides. My gripes are a few lines that slip into brochure language, one 'examples of each setting' claim the page doesn't deliver on, and one sentence in the cost section I had to read twice.

journey.quote: Take them in that order and each one narrows the next.
journey.reaction: A sequence I can put in a spreadsheet. Nobody's tried to sell me a view yet.

Every other FAQ answer is measured, then this one opens like an ad. The facts underneath are fine, and the body already tells me the downside: above about 60 seated you're into standing receptions or splitting spaces. Say that here and drop the cheerleading.

journey.quote: Many couples marry legally in Australia first and hold the symbolic ceremony on the island.
journey.reaction: 'Many' compared to what? It's probably true, but it's the sort of word I test. 'Some couples' says the same thing.

journey.section: What shapes the cost of a Santorini wedding
journey.quote: At venues such as Grace Hotel, a wedding planner is required for every wedding, so their fee belongs in the plan from the start.
journey.reaction: That's the catch I look for, named against a real venue. Useful to know before I compare planners.

journey.section: What shapes the cost of a Santorini wedding
journey.quote: Grace Hotel's venue fee includes exclusive use of the event spaces you choose, rather than the hotel.
journey.reaction: Exactly the fine print that would bite on the day. Good.

journey.section: What shapes the cost of a Santorini wedding
journey.quote: Where your date falls in the season, and whether it is a weekday, changes what is free and on what terms.
journey.reaction: 'Free' as in available, or free of charge? In a cost section I read it as no charge and then thought, which bit is free? I think it means available.

journey.section: Weather by month from official station data
journey.quote: The figures below are for Naxos, the nearest official station, so read them as a guide to the neighbourhood rather than a forecast for the caldera.
journey.reaction: Upfront about the limits of its own numbers. Most wedding sites would have just written 'Santorini weather' over somebody else's data.

journey.section: Heat, wind and wildfire advice for travellers
journey.quote: Greece is in an active seismic zone, with earthquakes and volcanic activity, including near Santorini.
journey.reaction: A wedding business telling me about earthquakes in its own destination guide, and telling me to keep insurance in place. That's the opposite of hiding the catch.

journey.section: Step 3: Choose your setting and venue type
journey.quote: The six venues below are examples of each setting, not a ranking.
journey.reaction: 'Not a ranking' is the right thing to say. But then the beach section has no venue at all, so it isn't an example of each setting. Small thing, but I notice when a page doesn't do what it just said.

journey.quote: Santorini's beaches are unlike anywhere else in Greece: black, red and white sand, multicoloured pebbles and steep cliffs.
journey.reaction: 'Unlike anywhere else in Greece' is travel-brochure stuff. The colours of the sand make the point without it.

journey.quote: Its terraces look out over the caldera, a setting made for vows at sunset.
journey.reaction: Every other venue line is capacity and facts. This one is mood. Tell me the capacity question instead, or just stop at the view.

journey.section: Step 4: Size your guest list against capacity and rooms
journey.quote: Check your guest list against the seated number for each space, not the standing one.
journey.reaction: Sensible, and the capacity table is the most useful thing on the page. Seated and standing side by side, by area. That's going straight in my spreadsheet.

journey.section: Step 3: Choose your setting and venue type
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Mid-page CTA, but it comes after a fair bit of evidence and doesn't oversell. Fine. Doesn't make me click yet.

journey.section: Step 7: Lock in the house rules in writing
journey.quote: Get the answers in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread.
journey.reaction: Someone who's clearly seen a vendor go back on a WhatsApp promise. That's the advice I'd have wanted last time.

journey.quote: Before you sign with any venue, get written answers to each of these:
journey.reaction: The whole checklist goes to every venue on our list. Practical, no fluff.

journey.section: Plan your Santorini wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. It still doesn't tell me whether you take a cut from the venues, but at least there's a fee agreed up front rather than buried in the supplier quotes.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee worked out, and what exactly does it cover?
If a venue like Grace Hotel requires a planner, does Wedded Concierge count as that planner, or is it a second fee?
Is the first conversation free, and what do I get out of it?
Is there a real Santorini wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: Its terraces look out over the caldera, a setting made for vows at sunset.
turn_offs_found.why: The rest of the venue entries give me capacities, spaces and terms. This line gives me a mood, and mood is what I discount when I'm comparing three planners side by side.

turn_offs_found.quote: Santorini's beaches are unlike anywhere else in Greece: black, red and white sand, multicoloured pebbles and steep cliffs.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Unlike anywhere else in Greece' is a superlative with nothing behind it. The list of sand colours already makes the point, so the claim adds nothing but a reason to raise an eyebrow.
It's the one FAQ answer that reads like a pitch. The page is honest elsewhere that capacity tops out around 60 seated on the caldera, so leaving that out of the answer makes it feel one-sided.

turn_offs_found.quote: Many couples marry legally in Australia first and hold the symbolic ceremony on the island.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Many' is a claim about other people's behaviour stated as fact. 'Some couples' costs nothing and doesn't make me wonder where the number came from.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the Step 9 booking checklist and the capacity table, to send to the venues on our list
Both sets of parents: the flying and ferry section, so they know about the stairs and the wind

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [plan your Santorini wedding with a Wedded Advisor]
cta_reaction.why: The page earned it: dated travel advice, honest weather data, real venue catches, a checklist I'll actually use. The CTAs come after evidence and don't oversell. What holds me back is the same as with every planner: do you take a cut from the venues, and how is the fee worked out? The fee-in-writing line helps, but it doesn't answer that.

top_3_changes: Fix the setting promise: 'The six venues below are examples of each setting' is not true for Beach venues, which names none. Either reword (for example 'examples of most of these settings') or name a beach example if one is available.
In the cost section, change 'changes what is free and on what terms' to 'changes what is available and on what terms', so 'free' is not read as 'free of charge'.

Strip the four brochure lines: cut 'a setting made for vows at sunset', drop 'unlike anywhere else in Greece', replace the FAQ opener 'Very.' with a straight answer that includes the 60-seated ceiling, and change 'Many couples' (and 'Plenty of couples' in Step 1) to 'Some couples'. (Commission, fee model and a free first call would also help, but those are deferred business details, so nice-to-have.)

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and costs first, looked for catches, superlatives, fee model and commissions
No invented brand facts; commission, fee model, planner overlap and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (image slots, fact tags, CTA markers) ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'not published' explanations

open_questions.question: The page says Grace Hotel requires a planner for every wedding. For this persona that raises whether Wedded Concierge fills that role or adds a second fee. Is that in scope this round, or deferred with the other business details?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via a Google search for 'santorini wedding' with Santorini on the shortlist while comparing three planners.
No prices on the page, including the cost section, is by design and not penalised.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not assessed.
